item.description: (Photo by Scott Strazzante/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) The San Francisco 49ers will be without Mike Evans for the first time this season. According to warm-ups, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins will start on the outside. Christian Kirk likely plays the slot, with Jacob Cowing sprinkled in there. When these teams met a season ago, Christian McCaffrey ran for 129 yards with Mac Jones as the starter. He also had seven receptions for 72 yards. In that game, George Kittle was held without a target. It’s national tight end week, so we think Kittle might be peppered with a target or five on Sunday. The wideouts who were targeted last year were Jauan Jennings — who had 31 yards on seven targets — Skyy Moore, and Kendrick Bourne. The 49ers only scored 20 points in that game, but it gives you an idea of how this offense can function, even without its starting quarterback, against the defense they’ll face today. Something tells me the 49ers will look like the 49ers once the game is decided. Can they contain Atlanta? Probably. This game could be high-scoring, as most 49ers games are.

item.description: Fred Warner of the San Francisco 49ers eyes the quarterback during the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on Oct. 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, Calif. The latter play saw referees initially throw a flag on Warner for the tackle on Chig Okonkwo. But after a discussion, the penalty flag was picked up and waved off. So depending on how you look at it, Warner got away with one in that instance. item.title: Where is Ohio State football ranked in Coaches poll after Week 8?
item.description: Ohio State football remains near the top of the US LBM Coaches Poll . OSU had a break in its schedule in Week 8 of the college football season. The Buckeyes defeated No. 4 Indiana 19-15 on Oct. 17 and jumped three spots to No. 2 in last week's Coaches poll as No. 1 Georgia and No. 2 Notre Dame dropped following their first losses. Ohio State sat below Miami in both Week 7 major polls . In AP voting, Ohio State also ranked behind BYU, who took down Notre Dame 28-24. While Miami maintained its top ranking with a 52-23 win over Pittsburgh on Oct. 24, BYU suffered a double-overtime loss to UCF, giving Ohio State a chance to move up in the AP poll, released at 2 p.m. The Cougars fell six spots to No. 9 in the Coaches poll. The Buckeyes return to action against No. 25 USC on Oct. 31 for their first game without starting quarterback Julian Sayin. The second-year starter is out indefinitely, and freshman Luke Fahey is the leading candidate to start in Los Angeles. Ohio State football ranking: US LBM Coaches Poll Ohio State earned 1,767 points, its most since getting 1,801 after Week 1, and six first-place votes to secure the No. 2 spot for the second straight week. Miami ranks No. 1 with 1,839 points and 67 first-place votes. USC tumbled 10 spots after recording its second loss of the season on Oct. 24, falling 24-7 to unranked Wisconsin. item.title: England lose to Pakistan after stunning Shadab ton
item.description: Haris Rauf (back) and Shadab Khan (front) shared a record 10th-wicket partnership to defeat England [Reuters] One-day international tri-series, Lahore England 241 (46.4 overs): Duckett 105 (111), Shaheen 4-46 Pakistan 243-9 (47.1 overs) : Shadab 113* (96), Overton 3-43 Pakistan won by one wicket Scorecard England somehow lost another one-day international from a seemingly unbeatable position thanks to an improbable last-wicket stand by Pakistan in Lahore. Three days after conceding 430 to lose to Sri Lanka, Harry Brook's side were beaten despite reducing Pakistan to 154-9 in pursuit of 242. Shadab Khan was the engineer of Pakistan's unlikely win, striking a quite brilliant unbeaten 113 - the highest score by a number eight in an ODI. He was supported by Haris Rauf, Pakistan's number 11 contributing seven to the unbroken 10th-wicket partnership of 89 - comfortably a new record for a last-wicket pair to win an ODI. In barely believable scenes, Shadab was given out lbw to Gus Atkinson on 97, with 21 runs still required. The players shook hands before Shadab called for a speculative review. DRS found a tiny inside edge and, reprieved, he watched Rauf belt debutant Henry Crocombe down the ground for the winning boundary with 17 balls to spare. It means England are all but out of the tri-series - their exit will be confirmed if Sri Lanka beat Pakistan on Tuesday. A second implosion in as many matches is hugely concerning for England, who looked to be on course for victory despite being bowled out for only 241. Ben Duckett made a fine 105 - only the opener, Sam Curran and Gus Atkinson passing 20 in blameless conditions. Nevertheless, England were well on course thanks to a collectively relentless display from their bowlers. Jamie Overton bowled his 10 overs in one spell for 3-43. Then came Shadab and another baffling defeat for England, who could be out before they play their final game against Sri Lanka on Thursday. Tournament experience teaching England to lose With less than a year to go to the World Cup, this tri-series was designed to give England experience of the pressure and permutations of tournament play. In a matter of days, they have gone through two extreme situations, both ending in crushing defeats. What linked both matches was England's powerlessness to salvage the situation once the momentum turned against them. If anything, the finish to this match was more dramatic than Sri Lanka pulling off the second-highest chase in ODI history . In the heat of the tight finish, Rauf had to be pulled away from a confrontation with England's Will Jacks when a Sam Curran bouncer was not called wide, while Rauf could also have been run out by Tom Banton's flick from mid-on when 18 were still required. Shadab expertly farmed the strike - Rauf faced only 19 deliveries in a stand that lasted 80 balls. Rauf defended his first 18 balls then cut loose to his 19th, hammering Crocombe for four then running away and throwing his bat in the air to begin the joyous celebrations. On Sunday, the bowlers were on course to mask the deficiencies of the batters, then wilted when it mattered. This loss means encouraging performances from Duckett and Overton will be forgotten. For Duckett, this was a much-needed score at time when questions have been asked about his position. Overton was superb, the first England seamer to bowl 10 consecutive overs in an ODI since 2017. But, when England needed inspiration to take the last wicket, they were found wanting. Maybe the pace of Archer or mystery of Rashid would have made the difference. They crowded the bat for Rauf, tried to defend against Shadab and held countless meetings. Heads dropped, plans failed and England were not good enough. Super Shadab wins it for Pakistan To focus only on England does a disservice to Shadab, who played a knock for the ages, one of the greatest by a Pakistan batter in an ODI. The all-rounder had been left out of the first two matches of this series. After bowling seven overs with his leg-spin, he arrived to bat when his team were in disarray at 103-6, then left as a hero. Shadab was unflappable in the face of such a monumental task, supported by the fiery Rauf. In a 96-ball stay, Shadab expertly picked his moments to attack, pouncing when England erred. He hit five sixes and 13 fours. Rauf batted for 70 minutes, more than two times his previous longest stay in an ODI. Only once before had he faced more deliveries. As tension rose, so did the tempers - Joe Root had to step in to guide Rauf away from Jacks. Rauf had the last word, but this will be remembered as Shadab's match. item.title: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton: Isak goal helps extend winning run as Reds climb to fourth
item.description: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton: Isak goal helps extend winning run as Reds climb to fourth Liverpool beat Brighton & Hove Albion 2-0 at Anfield to make it four wins in a row in all competitions and climb to fourth in the Premier League . It was also Liverpool's first league win at Anfield since April, ending a run of five home games and six months without one. Andoni Iraola's side now sit within a point of third-placed Brighton. Liverpool started brilliantly with a high-press putting the visitors under pressure. However, the first real chance fell to the Seagulls. Brighton's Yasin Ayari blazed over from a Pascal Gross cut-back in the 14th minute, and the squandered opportunity was soon punished. Just three minutes later, Florian Wirtz's low strike went in off Gross to put Liverpool ahead. Moments later, the lead was doubled. Bradley Barcola charged down an attempted clearance from Olivier Boscagli, brushed off a challenge and curled a cross into the path of Alexander Isak, who finished from close range. Brighton grew back into the game after Liverpool's quick-fire start, and Ayari struck the post in the 36th minute, before Verbruggen tipped away a powerful drive from Ronald Araujo at the other end. The Seagulls saw plenty of the ball after the break but were unable to find a route past the home side's defence. Brighton had not conceded in all competitions for over nine hours before kick-off and arrived as the Premier League's leading scorers with 23 goals. Liverpool, by contrast, had scored just nine in their first seven league games. The one Liverpool concern was an injury to Wirtz, who had been bright. He was replaced by Trey Nyoni on 65 minutes after stretching to halt a Brighton attack. Liverpool have now won four consecutive games in all competitions, a run that has followed a 3-0 defeat to Manchester City earlier this month. item.title: 0 punches, 1 error leading to goal: Senne Lammens’ struggles continue as United suffer 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth
item.description: 0 punches, 1 error leading to goal: Senne Lammens’ struggles continue as United suffer 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth Manchester United suffered a 3-0 defeat at the hands of Bournemouth in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Sunday, 25 October. Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson found the back of the net as the Red Devils succumbed to their sixth defeat in 12 games across competitions this season. Michael Carrick made four changes to the team that endured a humiliating 4-1 defeat at the hands of Como in midweek in the Champions League. Leny Yoro replaced Matthijs de Ligt at the back, partnering Harry Maguire at the heart of the defence. Diogo Dalot retained his place at right-back, but Ayden Heaven was stationed at left-back, replacing Noussair Mazraoui. In midfield, Carlos Baleba was handed his Premier League debut, starting alongside Andrey Santos. Youri Tielemans was pushed into the No. 10 role, with Bruno Fernandes dropping down to the bench. Mason Mount retained his position in attack, alongside Bryan Mbeumo, who operated in the No. 9 role, but Amad replaced Matheus Cunha. United were torn apart by Bournemouth United had a slow start to the game as Bournemouth threatened to score on multiple occasions. They eventually got their breakthrough in the 38th minute when Rayan found the back of the net. If the Red Devils supporters were hoping to see a fight-back from the team, their expectations were dashed by an error by Yoro. Adrien Truffert stole the ball off the Frenchman and set up Marcus Tavernier to double the lead for the visitors. Carrick’s team went into the break with the scores at 2-0 and the Englishman decided to bring on Matheus Cunha in place of Tielemans ahead of the second half. However, the Cherries continued to threaten to score, prompting Carrick to replace Heaven with Lisandro Martinez. Unfortunately, Lammens misjudged a long ball in the 71st minute and came a long way off his line and gifted Evanilson an opportunity. The Brazilian made no mistake and put the ball into the back of the open net to make it 3-0 and kill the game. Lammens’ poor form continues Lammens was exceptional last season but has appeared short of confidence after a poor 2026 FIFA World Cup. The Belgian has started all but one game this season for United, but has looked a shadow of the player who became the darling of the Old Trafford faithful last campaign. Against Bournemouth, the 24-year-old had 43 touches of the ball, and attempted 36 passes with a mere 75% passing completion rate. He did register one key pass, but only three of his 12 long balls made it to a team-mate. Lammens made just one save in the game and registered two high claims. However, he also committed an error which led to Evanilson’s goal. Page 1 of 2 1 2 Final Thoughts Lammens showed last season that he has the attributes to become a key figure for United. The Belgian’s recent form, as such, should be a cause for concern.

item.title: Carrick on the brink as Man Utd misery mounts, Isak stars for Liverpool
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick (Darren Staples) Michael Carrick was pushed to the brink of being sacked after Manchester United slumped to a miserable 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth, while Alexander Isak extended his hot streak in Liverpool's 2-0 win against Brighton on Sunday. Carrick's bold decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes backfired as defeat stretched United's winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. For the third time in four seasons, the Cherries won by a three-goal margin at Old Trafford as strikes from Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson secured a fully deserved victory for Marco Rose's side. Fernandes was critical of Carrick's tactics in a 4-1 Champions League thrashing at Como on Wednesday. The United boss said the decision to leave out last season's Premier League Player of the Year was a "purely football" driven, but it was hard to believe Fernandes was not being punished as he was left on the bench for the entire match. Carrick was taunted with chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning" from the Bournemouth fans. But on this evidence, dismissing another manager is far from a quick fix for a club that has fallen dramatically from grace since Alex Ferguson's retirement after winning their most recent English title 13 years ago. A strong finish to last season during Carrick's interim spell in charge secured third place in the Premier League. Yet with just one win against promoted Ipswich, United have taken just seven points from eight league games so far this season -- their lowest tally at this stage of a season since 1986-87. item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick reacts ahead of the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester United and AFC Bournemouth at Old Trafford. The former Red Devils midfielder’s position was already hanging in the balance as their poor start to the season was compounded by Wednesday’s calamitous 4-1 loss at Champions League upstarts Como. Under-fire Carrick spoke with defiance and hope ahead of hosting Bournemouth, but Sunday’s meek loss extended United’s winless run to an eighth straight match in all competitions and leaves their boss facing the sack. Rayan and Marcus Tavernier scored avoidable first-half goals for the well-drilled Cherries at Old Trafford, where home fans displayed a banner reading “standards” as the players trudged off at the break. Roy Keane, Eric Cantona and Bryan Robson featured on the sign brought out of storage for a match that current captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped for days after his critique of Carrick’s approach in Italy. The head coach claimed it was a “pure football” decision rather than punishment, but he remained on the bench throughout a tepid second half that saw Evanilson punish a wandering Senne Lammens. item.title: Charles Leclerc reacts to Ferrari fear: 'We know what line not to cross'
item.description: Motorsport photo One of the common denominators of Ferrari ’s mid-season, besides not translating practice pace into qualifying, has been its drivers’ tendency to trip over one another on track. More often, this has come in the form of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton not being as collaborative as they could be when they encounter each other on track while running on opposed strategies. But it has also involved points-scoring opportunities lost in a more direct manner, such as when Leclerc ushered Hamilton into the gravel trap on the opening lap of the Italian Grand Prix. Leclerc and Hamilton qualified fourth and fifth at the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas (COTA), a track where the first corner – a sharp left at the top of the hill – is a notorious pinch point. Last year two of the championship protagonists, McLaren ’s Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri , collided there at the start of the sprint race, handing title rival Max Verstappen a clear run to victory. Fourth and fifth means the Ferrari drivers aren’t directly alongside one another on the grid, but they are still close enough to become entangled as the field squeezes into Turn 1 on the opening lap. Motorsport.com understands that, after the Italian GP incident, team boss Frederic Vasseur held private clear-the-air talks between the two drivers. But, speaking after qualifying in Austin, Leclerc insisted that there have been no specific rules laid down for what happens at COTA’s Turn 1. “No, we know what the line is not to cross,” he said. “And again I think we've got some occasions throughout the year where I've crossed it, Lewis has crossed it, and we don't want to see that – so this is clear.” There are actually several parallels between the Turn 1 incident at Monza between Leclerc and Hamilton, and the McLaren drama at COTA last season. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It took half a season, but the college football coaching carousel is turning. Three Power 4 coaching jobs are open heading into Week 9. Maryland fired Mike Locksley, NC State parted ways with Dave Doeren and Baylor moved on from Dave Aranda. That means there is one opening in the ACC, Big Ten and Big 12 for 2027, and there promises to be more vacancies as the coaching carousel heats up in the second half of the season. It continues to be a wild year in the coaching ranks. Sporting News takes a closer look at all the coaching changes in 2026. MORE: College football rankings after Week 8 College football coaching changes 2026 Dave Aranda, Baylor Fired (Oct. 25): On.3 com's Pete Nakos reports Baylor fired Aranda . The Bears lost 25-24 to Kansas on Oct. 24, part of a 4-3 start that included back-to-back losses in Big 12 play. Aranda, 50, a former defensive coordinator at LSU and Wisconsin, struggled after Baylor finished 12-2 and reached the Sugar Bowl in the 2021 season. Aranda had a 40-40 record at Baylor. Dave Doeren, NC State Fired (Oct. 24): NC State announced it was parting ways with Doeren , 54. Doeren was fired one day after a 31-28 loss to Stanford dropped the Wolfpack to 3-4 on the season. Doeren, who took over in 2013, had a 98-73 record in 14 seasons with the program, and NC State made 10 bowl appearances. MORE: Philip Rivers among potential Wolfpack replacements Mike Locksley, Maryland Fired (Oct. 21): The Terrapins parted ways with Locksley , 56, after a 2-5 start in the Big Ten. Locksley took over at Maryland in 2019 and had a 39-54 record. Locksley led the Terps to three bowl victories, but Maryland had a 10-21 record with a 2-20 record in conference play after the Big Ten expanded to 18 teams. item.title: Liverpool 2–0 Brighton: Ronald Araújo Dominates in Anfield Victory
item.description: Liverpool 2–0 Brighton: Ronald Araújo Dominates in Anfield Victory Liverpool 2–0 Brighton – Premier League Man of the Match Ronald Araújo Liverpool FC Ronald Araújo delivered an outstanding performance as Liverpool secured a 2–0 victory over Brighton at Anfield, demonstrating exactly why the club’s option to sign him permanently could become such an important consideration at the end of the season. The on-loan defender was superb throughout the first half, combining defensive authority with an impressive contribution going forward. At right-back, he was an absolute rock in his own third, using his physicality, strength and positional awareness to deal with Brighton’s attacking threats. He looked assured in his decision-making and rarely allowed his opponents the opportunity to gain an advantage. What made Araújo’s performance particularly impressive was his ability to influence the game at both ends of the pitch. His defensive work provided Liverpool with a solid foundation, but his willingness to carry the ball forward also helped the Reds establish their attacking momentum. The opening goal was a perfect example. Araújo drove forward powerfully before laying the ball across the area, initiating the move that eventually resulted in Florian Wirtz’s effort finding the net. It was an important contribution that demonstrated the additional dimension he can offer from right-back. He is not simply a defender who can be relied upon to do the basics; he has the athleticism and confidence to change the course of a game. After the interval, Araújo continued to impress defensively, helping Liverpool maintain their clean sheet as Brighton looked for a route back into the contest. His performance was built on consistency, strength and a determination to win his individual battles. With an option to buy at the end of the season, Liverpool will surely be encouraged by what they are seeing. If Araújo maintains this level, it will be increasingly difficult to argue against making his move permanent. The Reds need reliable defenders who can cope with the physical demands of the Premier League while contributing to the team’s attacking play, and he is showing that he can offer both. Cody Gakpo also deserves recognition for another excellent display. He appears to have found a new lease of life under Andoni Iraola, looking more powerful, energetic and purposeful than he has at times since Liverpool’s title-winning season. His movement and work rate gave Brighton plenty to consider and added another dimension to the home side’s forward play. However, Araújo was the standout performer. His defensive solidity, physical presence and contribution to the opening goal made him a deserving Man of the Match. My pre-match prediction was Liverpool 2–1 Brighton, but the Reds went one better defensively to secure a 2–0 victory. Araújo played a major role in that success, and performances like this will only strengthen the case for keeping him at Anfield beyond this season.

item.title: Warriors honor Bay Area sports reporter Michael Wagaman
item.description: Credit: NBC Sports After Michael Wagaman passed away in early August, Dallas Braden took time to tribute him during his call of the Athletics’ game on NBC Sports Bay Area and California. Wagaman had covered Bay Area sports teams since 1996, including for the Associated Press, and freelanced for NBC Sports Bay Area and California at the time of his death. “He will be sorely missed,” Braden said , in part. “I know there’s a lot of writers across the Bay Area today who are mourning the loss of a man who has meant so much to them.” More than two months later, Wagaman is still sorely missed , and the Golden State Warriors mourned him during their home opener on Friday. The Warriors placed a jersey, a photo, a bouquet of flowers, and a placard in Wagaman’s honor in press row. The Warriors are honoring longtime reporter Michael Wagaman in press row tonight https://t.co/uQ7R2u6fbe — Warriors on NBCS (@NBCSWarriors) October 24, 2026 “Nice tribute by the Warriors to the legendary Mike Wagaman who wrote so many great stories from that seat,” wrote Tim Kawakami of the San Francisco Standard. “Thank you so much, wonderful @WarriorsPR! We all dearly miss him,” wrote Janie McCauley of the Associated Press. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr spoke highly of Wagaman in August, according to Susan Slusser of the San Francisco Chronicle . “Wags always stood out for his incredible personality and his ability to make people laugh,” Kerr said. “No matter what he was going through, he always brought great energy to the room. You knew when Wags was there. We’re really going to miss him.” Cal Athletics, the San Francisco Giants, and the San Francisco 49ers previously honored Wagaman after his death. In Memory of Mike “Wags” Wagaman We will forever miss Wags’ hearty laugh and ever-present positivity in our press box. Saturdays at Memorial won’t be the same without him. With deepest sympathies, Cal Athletics https://t.co/nlUUXfHs5v — CalFootballPR (@calfootballpr) September 5, 2026 The Giants held a pregame moment of silence to honor a pair of Bay Area legends, Michael Wagaman and Don Nelson https://t.co/loWeVievVg — SF Giants on NBCS (@NBCSGiants) August 9, 2026 #49ers hold a moment of silence in the press box for Mike Wagaman. — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) August 14, 2026 Four years ago, Wagaman’s son created a GoFundMe after Wagaman underwent emergency surgery to remove a brainstem tumor. Wagaman died at his Vallejo home on Aug. 7. He was 59. His cause of death has not been publicly confirmed. item.title: ‘Unfortunate mistake’: Knicks respond to ‘cruel’ championship ring confusion
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Brenden Willsch-Imagn Images On Tuesday, the New York Knicks celebrated their third NBA championship, and their first in more than half a century, in typical fashion, as the banner was raised and rings were presented at their opening-night game at Madison Square Garden. However, some Knicks staff members were left annoyed and ringless. According to a report from The Athletic , the Knicks’ assistant coaches received ring boxes during the ceremony but didn’t actually get rings. On top of that, many longtime Madison Square Garden employees reportedly won’t get rings at all, and some of them were targeted with a fake ring offer that turned out to be a cybersecurity ploy . On Friday, SNY reporter Ian Begley posted a statement from MSG that attempted to clarify the situation. “The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers,” an MSG spokesperson said, via Begley . “MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack. Using the rings as a lure to gain employees’ attention was an unfortunate mistake.” On Saturday, with criticism of owner James Dolan and the organization as a whole continuing to pile up, MSG released another statement. “There is a great deal of misinformation regarding the championship rings,” an MSG spokesperson said, via Begley . “The plan has always been to distribute more than 275 rings and jewelry to the people in the organization who were part of last season’s success. As is common with many teams, the players were always supposed to get their rings as part of the opening night ceremony, and then everyone else will receive theirs in about 4-6 weeks. “Regarding the phishing email, the process of securing and reminding our employees to protect our IP was not a mistake, but the choice to use the ring to do so was a mistake, and we apologize to our employees and the fans. Winning the championship was a great moment for all New Yorkers. Those who choose to focus on the negative are missing the joy that comes with the team’s accomplishment.” You can only assume the Knicks are looking to put the ring talk behind them, especially as they start their 2026-27 season 0-2. item.title: New York Jets discussion: Week 7 live chat during the Dolphins game
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: Tyrel Dodson #25 of the Miami Dolphins intercepts a pass intended for Mason Taylor #85 of the New York Jets during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last week the New York Jets failed to take advantage of an opportunity to get to .500 on the season and move into 2nd place in the AFC East when they lost a close game to the New England Patriots. The Jets got to within a touchdown with more than seven minutes remaining in the game. Then the Patriots, behind a makeshift offensive line missing most of their starters, put together a soul crushing, clock crunching, game sealing drive in which they basically ran the ball right down the Jets’ throats, and the Jets were helpless to stop it. It was a humiliating end to a pretty good overall performance by the Jets. The loss gave the Jets a 2-4 record on the season. Today the Jets are home at MetLife Stadium as they try to get back on the winning track against a winless Miami Dolphins team. Kickoff is scheduled for shortly after 1 PM EDT. The Dolphins have had a challenging schedule to start the 2026 season. They have yet to face a team with a losing record. The Jets will be their first such opponent. Coming off a tough loss against a division rival, the Jets could be set up for a letdown against the Dolphins. It’s up to the coaches and players to make sure that doesn’t happen. The Dolphins have dismantled the Jets on a regular basis in recent years. They have won 16 of the last 20 games played between these two teams. If the Jets want to compete for a playoff spot that will need to change. The Dolphins are a team in the midst of a clear tank. The Jets are the better, more talented team, and they are getting back close to full strength after a string of injuries hurt the team in the early part of the season. Can the Jets take care of business at home today? We’ll find out soon enough. It’s the Jets and the Dolphins in game 7 of the 2026 season. Enjoy the game everyone.

item.title: Lakers 1st-Round Draft Pick Floated as Trade Piece
item.description: Cameron Carr #43 of the Los Angeles Lakers Getty At 3-0 and with convincing wins behind them, things seem to be going as planned in Lakerland. But, maybe, if anything, the fast start from the Los Angeles Lakers can be viewed not as a reason to stick with the long-term plan to slowly build the roster around Luka Doncic going forward, but to accelerate the process by cashing in some young chips now for some immediate help. Maybe even a trade of rookie Cameron Carr. Carr has been out with an oblique injury and has yet to make his NBA debut. He was a surprise dropper during the NBA draft and the Lakers were fortunate to scoop him up at No. 24, and he looked good back in the preseason opener, with 19 points. But he is a rookie, with a long way to go to earn a consistent role in the current rotation. If this team really is as good as it has looked coming out of the gate–and we have a long, long way to go, of course–might it not make sense to trade away Carr sooner rather than later, to bring in a backup big man or a big forward? Lakers Could Trade Cameron Carr for Immediate Help That was the topic floated by Lakers insider Jovan Buha of the “Buha’s Block” podcast. He suggested that the team, though still committed to young players Carr and Adou Thiero, could use one or both to try to pry away the likes of Herb Jones from the Pelicans or Dereck Lively II from the Mavericks. “You’re unlikely to get both of those guys. I would say it’s even unlikely they get one of those guys, or guys of that caliber, but that would be something to strive for, in my opinion,” Buha said. “The more I think about it, I am coming around to potentially trading Adou or Carr in the right deal.” It’s an interesting notion, especially considering how few assets the Lakers have to offer on the trade market. They have only three future second-rounders to put in a deal, and one first-round pick swap. It would be a risk, but if this team keeps winning, moving Carr might be their best path to quickly find depth for the roster. item.title: Thunder sign ex-Pelicans defensive menace with high-motor upside, release Otega Oweh amid injury
item.description: Thunder sign ex-Pelicans defensive menace with high-motor upside, release Otega Oweh amid injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Oklahoma City Thunder are once again one of the most exciting teams in the NBA, especially after coming off a Game 7 loss in the Eastern Conference Finals. Oklahoma City has started the season well, continuing to showcase its smothering defense. However, just before the season began, the unfortunate trend of Thunder rookies suffering season-ending injuries before making their debuts continued. “This is the fourth season out of five where a Thunder rookie has been ruled out for the year before debuting. 2022: Chet Holmgren (Lisfranc). 2024: Nikola Topic (ACL). 2025: Thomas Sorber (ACL). 2026: Otega Oweh (Achilles),” The Athletic’s Law Murray wrote. Oweh had a chance to work his way into the rotation and potentially become a contributor for Oklahoma City. Instead, the Thunder had to make the difficult decision to waive him following his injury. “The Oklahoma City Thunder made their first roster move of the 2026-27 regular season. And it's one that shouldn't be a shocker to anybody. They have waived Otega Oweh. He was on a two-way contract. This was purely a roster mechanism move. Oweh sustained a torn Achilles tendon in OKC's preseason,” USA Today’s Clemente Almanza wrote. Oklahoma City decided to waive Oweh after agreeing to a two-way contract with Micah Peavy, a former second-round pick who was released by the Memphis Grizzlies . “The Oklahoma City Thunder and Micah Peavy have agreed to a two-way deal, league sources told hoopshype. Peavy, the 40th pick of the 2025 NBA Draft, played in 61 games for the New Orleans Pelicans last season,” HoopsHype’s Michael Scotto wrote. The move could turn into an under-the-radar signing that eventually pays major dividends for Oklahoma City. Finding playing time on a talented roster like the Thunder's will be difficult, but injuries could open the door for Peavy to earn opportunities. Peavy brings a high motor, which is exactly what Oklahoma City wants from a young player joining its organization. Oweh's situation is unfortunate, but the Thunder had to make a difficult roster decision and bring in a player they believe can help the team moving forward. item.title: Pistons’ Jalen Duren not only out vs. 76ers, but hamstring injury will force him out weeks
item.description: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Pistons’ Jalen Duren not only out vs. 76ers, but hamstring injury will force him out weeks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After claiming the No. 1 seed in the East last season, the Detroit Pistons have picked up where they left off in the regular season by winning their first two games. They followed up their huge 22-point comeback over the Boston Celtics with a decisive victory over the Giannis Antetokounmpo-led Miami Heat. However, the Pistons have been dealt their first big setback of the new season: All-NBA center Jalen Duren is set to be sidelined for at least two weeks due to a right hamstring strain. Duren picked up the injury during the second quarter of their win over the Heat. He had already been ruled out for their upcoming game against the Philadelphia 76ers. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Duren was in the middle of a prolonged contract saga in the offseason. After a breakout regular season where he averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds and made 3rd Team All-NBA, he was in line for getting a max contract extension worth over $280 million. However, he struggled mightily in the playoffs, averaging just 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds over 14 games. That led to the Pistons offering him less than the max. As a result, Duren took his time signing an extension. In the end, though, he agreed to a five-year, $200 million deal. Duren had 22 points and nine rebounds in 28 minutes in his lone full game of the new season against the Celtics. After he left early against the Heat, backup Paul Reed got more playing time and delivered a 19-point, 11-rebound double-double. It remains to be seen whether Pistons coach JB Bickerstaff will decide to start Reed as a direct replacement for Duren or if he will opt for a smaller lineup. item.title: Ohio State’s QB Decision Point Arrives After Sayin Injury for Fahey, St. Clair
item.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - APRIL 18: Quarterback Luke Fahey #13 of Team Scarlet drops back to pass in the third quarter of the Ohio State Buckeyes Spring Game at Ohio Stadium on April 18, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) Getty The Ohio State Buckeyes are going to have a different quarterback this week, but who will it be at USC? That’s the question that Ohio State officially has to answer this week after Julian Sayin’s injury against Indiana. The Buckeyes got a bye on Oct. 24, but with that Saturday done, it’s game week for Ohio State as they prepare to return to action against the Trojans. Someone is going to be named the starting quarterback, potentially having earned the gig in practice, and then it’ll be up to them to keep the Buckeyes in College Football Playoff contention. The options are Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair. At some point this week, Buckeyes fans will learn how this competition has shaken out. Julian Sayin Injury Maybe a Jeremiah Smith injury would be just as costly, but a Sayin injury is clearly one Ohio State couldn’t afford. He’s a star quarterback who makes the Buckeyes’ offense go, and it’s not easy to replace a stud QB. Sayin hurt his right (throwing) arm against Indiana, and Ohio State coach Ryan Day has said that Sayin will be out “indefinitely.” The lack of a timeline is definitely a concern, and it sure makes it seem like the Buckeyes are going to have to deal with a backup for a long stretch going forward. Luke Fahey vs. Tavien St. Clair When Sayin left the game against Indiana, the Buckeyes went with Fahey as the replacement. He wasn’t asked to do much, though, as Ohio State held on by just inches when a would-be Nick Marsh touchdown catch instead featured a foot barely out of bounds. Fahey was a much less-heralded recruit than St. Clair, who was a five-star quarterback out of Bellefontaine, Ohio. Despite that, it seems Fahey was trusted at least a bit more in Bloomington. The Buckeyes will have spent their bye week figuring things out and will have to finalize it this week. They have to strike a balance between reliability and upside, because this is a team not just trying to tread water but one that wants to win a national title. If Sayin really is out for a long stretch, Ohio State can’t afford to get this wrong. There’s tons of skill all over the field for the Buckeyes, which helps, but quarterback remains the most important position in sports. Fahey or St. Clair will have to get Ohio State to the promised land if Sayin isn’t around to do it himself. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
